shortDescription: Shared ability AI for NPC pawns plus player autocast (in place, or walk into range and back), situational undrafted casting, and per-pawn psycast heat/psyfocus limits. Split out of Entad Framework; Entad and Bastle Framework use it as a soft dependency through gated compat assemblies.
body:
## What it is
The ability AI that used to live in Entad Framework (`Source/AbilityAI/`), now its own mod so Entad Framework and Bastle Framework share one copy. Namespace `AbilityAI`, keyed prefix `AAI_`, Harmony id `saintwacko.abilityai`. Builds 1.6 and 1.7 (LoadFolders, shared `Source/`, per-version csproj under `1.6/Source` and `1.7/Source`, `Source/AbilityAI.Build.csproj` builds both). Krafs refs; Harmony is the only hard dependency.

## How abilities opt in
An `AbilityAIExtension` on the AbilityDef naming a worker class (AoEHostile, AoEFriendly, SelfBuff, Movement, Cover, Recovery, TargetHostile, TargetFriendly, Defensive, Rescue, Calm, Interrupt, Firefighting). Several extensions per ability are allowed and are tried by priority. Each worker has a combat mode (InCombat default; Recovery OutOfCombat; Rescue, Calm, Firefighting Any), overridable per extension with `combat`. Royalty's combat psycasts get extensions from `Patches/AbilityAI_Royalty.xml`: FindMod Royalty, then one PatchOperationConditional per def. Friend or foe is decided by the worker's candidate list (ctx.Allies / DownedAllies / Enemies), never by the comps.

## Comp target checks (`CompAllowsTarget`)
Two vanilla comps refuse any player-faction caster in `AICanTargetNow`: GiveHediff (Painblock, Focus, Invisibility, Burden, ...) and FireBurst. While TryGiveJob evaluates a pawn under Control.Player (`curPlayer`, exposed to workers as `AbilityAIDriver.EvaluatingPlayer`), those comps are replaced by their non-player condition: GiveHediff → target is a pawn; FireBurst → target aims at the caster. Decided per runtime comp type by which type declares `AICanTargetNow` (cached). NPCs and BreakCasting colonists keep vanilla's answer. Tested with Entad Framework: works.

## Calm worker (Word of Serenity)
NPCs: aggressive breaks only (or any with `anyMentalState`), within the extension's maxRange (8 for Word of Serenity), skipping breaks with under `minBreakSeconds` (60) left.
Player casters, setting `CalmBreaks` (radio, default MajorAndExtreme): Aggressive only / Major and extreme (by the MentalBreakDef intensity, cached array by MentalStateDef index; psychotic wandering, tantrums, drug binges, sadistic rage, corpse obsession, plus all extreme) / Any. With anything but Aggressive, downed allies with a CatatonicBreakdown hediff are candidates too (vanilla's StopMentalState cures it, priced extreme). Undrafted player casters use `CalmRange` (default 20, slider 5 to 60, straight line) for touch abilities; drafted keep the extension's reach.

## Who casts
- Driver: a postfix on `Pawn_JobTracker.DetermineNextConstantThinkTreeJob`, normally only when the constant tree has nothing to do, at most once per 30 ticks per pawn (slower for idle undrafted player pawns), plus a global minimum gap.
- **Over the hostility response** (player pawns only): when the constant tree's result comes from `JobGiver_ConfigurableHostilityResponse` (Attack or Flee), the driver still evaluates and its cast replaces that job (the set-aside job is pooled with vanilla's guard). While a cast this AI started is running (CurJob.ability with jobGiver == the tree root), the hostility job is dropped so it can't cancel the cast, except a flee, which wins unless the warmup has begun or the cast targets a pawn hostile to the caster (a berserk friend). Without this, colonists on Attack/Flee never autocast near a threat.
- NPCs (hostile, non-hostile, animals, mechs; each toggleable): cast abilities a host hook claims, or any ability with an extension when "Also use abilities no mod claims" is on. Factionless casters build their enemy list from every spawned pawn hostile to them plus whoever they are fighting back against.
- NPC approach (setting "Walk into range", NPCs only).
- AoEFriendly targeted casts try up to 5 allies, most covered first.

## Player autocast
Modes per pawn and ability from a right-click on the gizmo (saved in the `AbilityAIAutocast` WorldComponent): Off, Stationary ("auto"), Full ("auto+", pawns with a drafter and abilities with `approachDistance`).
- **Drafted**: every worker, only while holding position or on AttackStatic.
- **Full walk**: walks into range, casts, walks back (or to new cover with `ReturnToCover`); re-issued up to 2 times.
- **Undrafted** (setting "Also while undrafted", default on), worker set by situation (`PlayerSet`): Safe always; Fleeing adds Movement and Recovery; All while fighting back and in combat. Never while lying down or carrying; only interrupts a fight job (queued to resume) or a casually interruptible job the player didn't order and that is not on the blocked-jobs list.
- **Undrafted check interval** (`UndraftedIntervalTicks`, default 250, 30 to 1200) unless `UndraftedNeedsQuickCheck` (fleeing, exit-map job with recent harm, or fighting back and in a fight). `PawnState.slowEval` lets drafting/fighting/fleeing cut the wait short.
- **Blocked jobs** (`AbilityAIBlockedJobs`, `Dialog_BlockedJobs`): 40 defaults (meals, recreation, gatherings, rituals, childcare, learning), saved as a diff from the defaults (`abilityAI_blockedJobsAdded` / `Removed`), resolved lazily into a `bool[]` by JobDef.index. Window from a button under the interval slider: every casualInterruptible JobDef except the fight jobs, checked first, search, "Checked only", reset. Tested: works.
- Animals: need `displayGizmoWhileUndrafted` on the ability.
- Player pawns in a mental break act as NPCs only with BreakCasting on.

## Psycast limits (per pawn)
Gizmo after vanilla's psyfocus one: "Max heat" and "Min focus" drag bars (5% steps), stored in the world component when non-default. `PsycastWithinLimits` skips a psycast that would pass the heat cap or drop psyfocus under the floor. Real Psycasts only; NPCs have no limits.

## Host API (soft-dependency contract)
Hosts keep all references in a compat DLL loaded via `IfModActive="saintwacko.AbilityAI"`.
- `AbilityAIHooks.Register(IAbilityAIHook)`: Claim/Veto/NoOpinion, Notify_AICast.
- `AbilityAIInfo.Register<T>(radius, hediff, stuns)`.
- `AbilityAIDriver.Handles(pawn, ability)`, `OthersStandDown(pawn, ability)`.
- `Valid/ValidIgnoringRange` apply the player comp rules only inside an evaluation.

## Vanilla stand-down
A postfix on `Ability.AICanTargetNow` returns false whenever `OthersStandDown` is true (setting, default on).

## Settings
enabled, per pawn kind, unclaimed, vanilla stand-down, NPC approach, player autocast, also while undrafted (+ interval slider + blocked jobs window), show marker, after-Full-cast destination, calming abilities end (3 radios) + undrafted calm range slider, break casting, min gap, dev debug log, reset.

## Autocast badge and marker
Badge "auto"/"auto+" on the gizmo; grey ring when the menu is available but mode is Off (`ShowMarker`); tooltip line via a `Command.DescPostfix` postfix.

## Handoffs
`.circinus/handoff/entad-framework.md`, `bastle-framework.md`, `player-autocast-plan.md` (steps 3 to 5 done), `next-steps.md` (bug fix, A, B done in builds 0020 to 0024). Builds 0025 to 0027: calm settings and casting over the hostility response, untested in game.
